data.description:
# Raise Qwen3 cache-ram to 40,960 MiB

Follow-up to LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW (which verified the 32,768 MiB cap on the
live post-deploy window) and LP-0MUYFC3C5004TCYN.

## Context

The 2026-10-12 post-32-GiB verification
(`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-12.json`) showed the cache is
still saturating under the current single-slot load:

- 18 evictions over ~4.7 d (1.28% of requests; 65 -> 18 vs the length-matched
  8 GiB window, a 72.9%/req reduction);
- 26.3% of cache-state samples above 90% of the 32,768 MiB cap (vs 22.0% at
  8 GiB);
- observed maximum 16 concurrently-retained prompts, cache peak 32,765.6 MiB
  (fully saturated).

`scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py --recommend` over that measurement derives
**40,960 MiB (40 GiB)**:

    per-prompt state 2,013 MiB x observed max 16 x 1.25 margin = 40,260 MiB
    -> round up to 40,960 MiB (holds ~20 prompts >= observed 16)

Headroom is safe (host available 79,248 MiB - 40,960 = 38,288 MiB, well above
the 12,743.7 MiB reserve = max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)), so the
`server_prompt_cache::alloc()` OOM fallback (`limit_size = 0.4 * size()`) is
not approached.

## Goal

As a proxy operator, raise the Qwen3 prompt-cache cap to the derived
40,960 MiB so the cache stops saturating and evicting session prefixes under
the single-slot load, with the derivation and headroom recorded.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` `cache-ram` raised 32768 -> 40960, with the
   derivation (per-prompt 2,013 MiB x observed max 16 x 1.25) and the
   2026-10-12 measurement reference recorded in the comment block.
2. Headroom invariant re-checked at 40,960 MiB: MemAvailable - 40960 >= reserve
   (reserve = max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)); the OOM fallback path is documented
   as avoided.
3. Deploy via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (never kill the proxy manually);
   confirm the spawned Qwen3 child carries `--cache-ram 40960` (and
   `--ctx-checkpoints 32`, no `--swa-full`).
4. `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` updated with the new cap, the derivation
   and the deploy evidence.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Changing `ctx-checkpoints` / `checkpoint-every-n-tokens` (kept at 32; the
  checkpoint term is not the lever, see `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`).
- Re-tuning routing cold/warm thresholds.
- The live post-deploy validation of this change (separate follow-up).

Discovered from: LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW

discovered-from:LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE

## Problem

During LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE (add 'explain names on first mention' rule to author.txt) it was confirmed that `proxy/prompts/author.txt` is **not** currently resolved by the proxy for the `author` alias.

- `proxy/config.yaml` author entry has no `system_prompt` block, and `proxy/prompt_resolver.py:resolve_system_prompt()` returns `None` when `model_cfg['system_prompt']` is absent.
- `resolve_system_prompt` is only called from `server.py` (debug endpoint) and `ui.py`; nothing else loads `author.txt`.
- No consumer in the repo or the `open_source_llm` wiki tooling references the file path.

## Impact

The author prompt content (including the new first-mention-explanation rule from LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE) has no effect through the proxy's auto-loading path.

## Proposed fix

Add a `system_prompt` block to the `author` model entry in `proxy/config.yaml`, e.g.:

```yaml
  author:
    ...
    system_prompt:
      mode: "prepend"   # confirm override vs prepend with the operator
      file: "proxy/prompts/author.txt"
```

Then add a test asserting the author entry resolves author.txt (e.g. via `resolve_system_prompt('author', model_cfg)` against the real config), and document the wiring in `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` / `proxy/README.md`.

## Open question

Confirm whether the wiki authoring client already sends author.txt as a client-supplied system message (making the proxy wiring unnecessary), or whether the proxy should auto-load it.
data.title: Wire proxy/prompts/author.txt into the author model system_prompt config

data.description:
**Parent:** LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI (When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer)
**Type:** task (verification) · **Priority:** high

## Problem

The proxy already emits the composed "All providers exhausted" retry contract
(`Retry-After` header + matching `retry_after` body field, stable `code`, no
over-long chain-hold), but the existing end-to-end test
(`proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`, from LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG) does
**not** pin the composed contract tightly enough to catch every regression:

- it asserts `retry_after > 0` and that the header matches the body, but never
  asserts the value **equals** the real soonest availability computed under a
  pinned clock (AC2);
- it exercises the generic `code: all_exhausted` path end-to-end, but the
  sole-cause time-window `code: outside_time_window` variant is asserted only
  against the response builder (`test_exhaustion_error_code.py`), not through
  the fallback chain with the retry timer (AC3);
- the client-recognition prose (`error == "All providers exhausted"`) and the
  bounded-hold guarantee are asserted, but not as one pinned regression for
  the retry timer (AC1, AC4, AC5).

## Change

Harden the end-to-end exhaustion test so the whole "no models available" retry
contract is pinned and fails if any part regresses. Extend the existing test
file — do **not** duplicate the window+quarantine or lease-denied scenarios.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Retry timer present and consistent:** A deterministic end-to-end test
  drives the in-process proxy with every provider unavailable and asserts the
  terminal `503` "All providers exhausted" response carries **both** a
  `Retry-After` HTTP header (integer delta-seconds) and a `retry_after` JSON body
  field, with the **same value**.
- **AC2 — Timeless truthfulness:** The asserted `retry_after` equals the real
  soonest availability (the maximum of cooldown durations, `available_times`
  window edges, and usage-limit reset times), is positive whenever a provider is
  genuinely blocked, and is `0` only when availability exists. The test pins the
  clock/value so the assertion is deterministic.
- **AC3 — Both exhaustion variants covered:** The verification covers the generic
  `code: "all_exhausted"` path and the time-window `code: "outside_time_window"`
  path (both are "All providers exhausted" 503s), asserting the same retry-timer
  contract on each.
- **AC4 — Client-recognition contract intact:** The response retains
  `error == "All providers exhausted"` and a stable `code`, and the existing
  exhaustion-contract tests still pass (additive-only; no prose/code change).
- **AC5 — No hold longer than the timer:** When a chain-hold would exceed the
  retry timer, the exhaustion response is surfaced immediately with the timer
  rather than held beyond it (bounded by `retry_after`). Verified in the same or
  a paired test.
- **AC8 — Full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`: reuse `_FixedDateTime`, `_DummyRequest`, the provider-state reset fixture and the `_record_hold` monkeypatch already in the file.
- Add a sole-cause window case with all providers outside `available_times` and no cooldown/quarantine, asserting `code == "outside_time_window"` plus the matching `Retry-After`/`retry_after`.
- For the window+quarantine case, pin the expected value (window edge in seconds under `_FixedDateTime`) and assert `retry_after == <expected>` exactly, that `_compute_retry_after` under the same clock equals it, and that the header equals the body string.
- Assert the `0` edge case (`_build_exhausted_response()` with no blockers → `retry_after == 0`).
- Keep determinism: monkeypatch `_hold_sleep` to record; assert no real sleep.
- No code change to `proxy/proxy/provider.py` is expected; if a genuine gap is found, raise a bug work item and record the blocking relationship instead of widening scope.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py` — the extended E2E retry-timer assertions (primary).
- `proxy/tests/test_honest_retry_after.py` — reuse its pinned-clock expectations for the window-edge arithmetic.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_retry_after_bound.py` — reference for the bounded-hold assertions.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only reference: `_compute_retry_after` (~2383), `_build_exhausted_response` (~3177), `_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (~3241).

## Deliverables

- Test diff with the pinned retry-timer assertions for both exhaustion variants and the bounded-hold guarantee.
- Recorded test-run output (targeted file + full suite) as evidence on this work item.
data.title: E2E retry-timer contract verification (all-exhausted + time-window)

**Parent:** LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI (When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer)
**Type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Problem

The proxy emits a truthful multi-hour `Retry-After` on the "All providers
exhausted" 503. Whether that timer is actually honoured depends on the
ContextHub client, which previously clamped every applied `Retry-After` to
60 s. The linked client item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM was created for that gap
(producer decision Q3a). The proxy item must record the cross-link and verify
that the client-side honouring landed, so the composed contract is
demonstrably intact from the client's perspective.

## Change

Record and verify the cross-repository link: confirm the ContextHub change
honours long server hints and record the evidence (file/line/default plus its
tests) on this work item. Do not edit the ContextHub repository from this
item; if a residual client gap remains, raise a new linked work item instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC6 — Client gap linked:** The ContextHub item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM exists and
  is referenced from this item, so the proxy's honest multi-hour timer can be
  honoured by the client rather than clamped to 60 s.
- The cross-link comment on this work item records the client-side evidence: `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` exposes `serverHintMaxDelayMs` (default 6 h) and no longer clamps a server hint to `maxDelayMs`, with covering tests named.
- Any residual client-side gap is raised as a new work item and recorded as a blocking/related link (not silently folded into this item).

## Minimal implementation

- Inspect the ContextHub recovery module and record the exact file, symbol, default value and covering test names as evidence.
- Add a comment on `LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI` with the cross-references and evidence, and the outcome of the verification (gap closed / residual gap).
- Confirm the ContextHub item in `WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` already references this proxy item; add a reciprocal note only if the item is still open.

## Dependencies

- None (cross-repository evidence gathering); may proceed in parallel with the test item.

## Key Files

- ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — `serverHintMaxDelayMs`, `calculateDelay` (read-only, not edited here).
- ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.test.ts` — long-hint coverage (read-only).
- `proxy/README.md` — referencing doc target for the client expectation (owned by the docs sibling item).

## Deliverables

- A verification comment on this work item with the cross-links and quoted client evidence.
data.title: Cross-link and verify ContextHub long Retry-After honouring

data.description:
**Parent:** LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI (When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer)
**Type:** docs · **Priority:** medium
**Depends on:** the E2E retry-timer verification test sibling (test-first ordering)

## Problem

`proxy/README.md` documents the exhaustion 503 contract, the client-facing
retry-timer cap (`server.max_retry_after_seconds`, default 3600 s) and the
chain-hold bound, but it does **not** state the retry contract as an
end-to-end-verified guarantee and does not state the client expectation (that
the ContextHub client honours the full advertised hint up to its own long
ceiling, rather than clamping to 60 s). Without this the verified contract is
not discoverable, and the relationship between the capped advertisement and
the client wait is ambiguous.

## Change

Update `proxy/README.md` (and the relevant `provider.py` comments) to state the
verified "no models available" retry contract and the client expectation,
pointing at the end-to-end verification test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, `proxy/README.md` (the exhaustion/retry
  contract section), and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- `proxy/README.md` states the verified contract explicitly (truthful `Retry-After` + matching `retry_after`, capped-advertisement vs unbounded-true-wait distinction, both `code` variants, bounded-hold guarantee) and names the end-to-end verification test as the regression guard.
- The README documents the client expectation (ContextHub honours the full advertised hint via `serverHintMaxDelayMs`, default 6 h, referencing WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM) without contradicting the advertisement-cap section, and records the docs/wiki scan outcome.

## Minimal implementation

- Edit the "All Providers Exhausted" section (~line 690) and the "Client-facing retry-timer cap" subsection to add a short "Verified retry contract" paragraph plus the client expectation.
- Add a one-line comment/docstring reference in `provider.py` naming `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`.
- Search `docs/` and the wiki for related exhaustion/retry pages; update or confirm no change needed and record the outcome.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the E2E retry-timer verification test item (document the verified contract only once it is pinned).

## Key Files

- `proxy/README.md` — exhaustion / retry contract sections (~line 690 and the "Client-facing retry-timer cap" subsection).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — comments on `_compute_retry_after` / `_build_exhausted_response` / `_build_time_window_exhausted_response`.

## Deliverables

- Updated README + code-comment diff.
- A short note recording the docs/wiki scan outcome.
data.title: Document verified no-models retry contract and client expectation
